tagline: Pre-Mughal Gujarati capital with hill temples, mosques and fortifications.

sections.title: Origins & History
sections.text: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, in the Panchmahal district of Gujarat, is a rare, largely unchanged medieval city that mixes Hindu and Islamic heritage. The site covers a landscape of hills, forts, palaces, mosques, tombs, step wells and water installations around Pavagadh Hill. Early settlement is associated with Hindu dynasties such as the Chavdas from the 8th century and later the Khichi Chauhan Rajputs. In 1484 Sultan Mahmud Begada captured the fort after a long siege, renamed the city Muhammadabad and made it his capital until the Mughal Humayun took it in 1535.

sections.title: Beauty & Atmosphere
sections.text: The beauty of the site lies in its setting and its variety. Spread across fields and forest, the monuments look natural in the landscape, and the stone architecture combines local Gujarati traditions of carved stone, pillars and brackets with Islamic arches, domes and minarets. The result is a distinctive regional Sultanate style that influenced later Indian mosque architecture.

sections.title: Architecture & Highlights
sections.text: The Jami Masjid, completed in the early 16th century, is among the most admired buildings, with a large courtyard, a tall entrance and graceful carved minarets. Other important monuments include the Sahar ki Masjid, the Kevda Masjid, the Nagina Masjid, the royal enclosure and the elaborate water systems that supplied the city. On top of Pavagadh Hill, which rises to around 800 metres, the Kalika Mata Temple is an active pilgrimage place, and nearby are Jain temples and fortified gates, reachable by steps or ropeway.

sections.title: Famous For
sections.text: Champaner-Pavagadh is celebrated as the only complete and unchanged Islamic pre-Mughal city in India, according to UNESCO. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2004.

visitor_tips: Visitors should plan most of a day because the monuments are spread out.
Wear sturdy shoes, carry water and consider visiting in the cooler months from about October to March.
Vadodara is the nearest large city and a convenient base.
Check current rules and access with official sources before travelling.
